title: Imaging Oxygen Dopants in Sr2CuO3+δ Superconducting Film by Multislice Electron Ptychography
content: Sr2CuO3+δ is a cuprate superconductor with a critical temperature, Tc, up to 95 K. The structural phase responsible for the high-Tc of this material has been studied extensively since its discovery [1], yet it remains unclear. A key issue concerns the location and distribution of oxygen within the lattice. While some studies suspect the oxygen vacancies reside within the Cu-O plane [2], others report oxygen vacancies occupy at the apical oxygen site [3]. Resolving this issue will provide insight on whether Cu-O planes are essential for high Tc in cuprate superconductors. Multislice electron microscopy (MEP) is well-suited for addressing this question because of its light-element sensitivity and remarkable lateral and depth resolutions [4], which has been successfully applied in nickelate superconductors [5].
